first.rationale: Two metrics (activation, onboarding completion) are down this quarter, and durable memory (memory_86, memory_31) shows onboarding simplification reliably lifts completion and activation without noted downside. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure but is explicitly flagged as harming 30-day retention and not to be generalized as a strategy, so it's excluded from this week's single experiment slot despite competitive urgency. Verifying memory_73's source confirms the retention tradeoff is real and not overstated before ruling it out, and verifying memory_86 confirms the onboarding lift is robust enough to justify the one available experiment slot given current declining metrics. Running onboarding simplification as a standard (not broad) experiment lets us address the activation/onboarding decline with a low-risk, previously validated lever while preserving optionality to address the competitive pricing threat separately once retention impact can be mitigated or better understood.
